name: X-linked Severe Syndromic Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Severe Syndromic Thoracic Aortic Aneurysm and Dissection

criteria.description: Presence of thoracic aortic aneurysm confirmed by imaging
Positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Presence of syndromic features including skeletal abnormalities and connective tissue manifestations
Identification of pathogenic variant in the implicated X-linked gene
History or evidence of thoracic aortic dissection

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diagnosis requires presence of thoracic aortic aneurysm, syndromic features, and positive family history consistent with X-linked inheritance.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing supports diagnosis but is not mandatory if clinical criteria are met.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically detected by imaging modalities such as echocardiography or CT angiography

pathognomonic.symptomName: X-linked inheritance pattern with male predominance
pathognomonic.notes: Family history often reveals affected males
searchTerms: X-linked inheritance with mostly males affected

pathognomonic.symptomName: Syndromic connective tissue abnormalities including skeletal deformities
pathognomonic.notes: Includes features such as joint hypermobility and pectus deformities
searchTerms: connective tissue problems with skeletal deformities
joint and bone abnormalities with connective tissue issues

common.notes: May present acutely with chest pain and hemodynamic instability
Chest wall deformities common in connective tissue disorders

occasional.notes: May result from aortic root dilation
Expansion of the dural sac around the spinal cord

rare.notes: Rare complication due to lung blebs

searchTerms: stroke and blood vessel nerve problems
neurological issues from blood vessel disease

laboratory: No specific laboratory biomarkers; routine labs typically normal
imaging: Echocardiography showing thoracic aortic aneurysm and possible valve abnormalities
CT or MRI angiography confirming aortic dilation and dissection
genetic: Pathogenic variants in the implicated X-linked gene (specific gene currently under investigation)
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with X-linked inheritance

redFlags: Acute chest or back pain suggestive of aortic dissection
Family history of sudden cardiac death in young males
